title: Cabuya adoption ledger
description: The state of one repository's adoption of the Cabuya Protocol, written to .cabuya/adoption.json. Two properties are structural rather than conventional: a conformance level exists only inside last_measured with the report digest that proves it, and the PII decision can only have been made by a human.

contract.description: The major.minor of this ledger contract. A reader from an older major reads and explains; it never writes.

publisher_id.description: The registry token, once one exists. Assigned once, never reassigned.

guide.description: The matched stack guide, as a pack-relative path.

target_level.description: What the adopter is aiming at. An aim, never a claim.

methodology.description: Who plans this adoption. Absent means nobody has been asked yet; the question is asked once.

id.description: The registry id from plan/methodologies.json, when the methodology is a known one.

entry_command.description: The command that starts a plan, as the adopter types it.

artifacts_path.description: Where the methodology keeps its plans and specs, repo-relative.

source.description: How this answer was reached: detected (a marker, confirmed by the human), declared (the human named it), dwp (DeepWorkPlan path), plan_mode (the agent's own planning mode).

pii_decision.description: The one mandatory human decision. decided_by is a constant: an agent cannot satisfy this schema on its own authority.

approved_columns.description: Column or field NAMES the human approved for publication. Names, never values.

steps.description: One entry per completed task from plan/tasks.json, in completion order.

last_measured.description: The only place a conformance level may exist — and only with the digest of the validator report that measured it. An offline run is not a measurement: mode offline forbids level entirely.

target.description: What the validator was pointed at: a URL for online, a repo-relative path for offline.

report_digest.description: sha256 of the validator's JSON report — the receipt that makes the level checkable.
